Lemma, forward: v in S(m) sends b=1 on every edge; a neighbour u with b(u->v)=1 is in S(m); a neighbour with b(u->v)=0 has h(u->v)=1, hence >= k-1 other incoming a's, and a(v->u)=1 because removing u's b=0 message leaves v's k b's; every w with a(w->u)=1 then gets h(u->w)=1 and lies in S(m), so u has k neighbours in S(m). Reverse: the lower messages (a: v in S with k other S-neighbours; b: v in S; h: v in S u N(S)) are a subsolution, the v in N(S) minus S case using that each S-neighbour w of v has |N(w) n S| >= k and v not in S; a subsolution lies below the greatest fixed point, so S is inside S(m*). Poisson recursion: child types 111/011/001/000 with probabilities p, q-p, s-q, 1-s thin into independent Poisson counts; A is inside B and Z is disjoint from B, so P(a)=d Q_k(cq), P(b)=d Q_(k-1)(cq), and b=0 with A>=k-1 is exactly Z>=1 with A>=k-1 (A>=k-1 forces B>=k-1), giving (1-d)Q_(k-1)(cp); the root has no parent, so its core probability is lim p_t. The finite-graph bound uses K inside S(m_t) for every t (monotone in m) and local weak convergence, upper direction only, as stated.
